prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1191; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver was named on the policy as a person who may NOT drive the car.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a rear-end collision at a traffic light. The claimant reports shoulder pain and confirmed they are not represented by a lawyer.
Entry 2: Police attended the scene and confirmed the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time of impact. The other driver's statement matches the sequence the claimant described.
Entry 3: Scene photos and two independent witnesses confirm the accident happened as described. Damage to the rear of the claimant's car is largely in line with the impact described.
Entry 4: Reviewed the policy and found the driver at the time is named as a person who may not drive the vehicle. Referred the file to the coverage team before any decision on the claim.
Entry 5: Vehicle records show no earlier damage, and nothing suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.
Entry 6: Initial medical assessment recorded a shoulder injury. The kind of injury and its force fit the crash well.
Entry 7: The claimant has added some small details in later calls, but the core account has stayed the same across each telling.
Entry 8: Medical history check shows no known earlier injury to the same shoulder area.
Entry 9: Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the claimant improved. The physician's notes describe a steady recovery.
Entry 10: Settlement review is on hold until the coverage team responds on the driver question. Will update the file once a decision is made.
